title: Holding and replying a child does not spoil them
summary: The milestone sheet says you will not spoil a child by holding or responding, and that cuddling lets the child feel safe and cared for.
body: The United States milestone sheet for 2-month page tells caregivers to devote time cuddling and holding the child so the child feels safe and cared for. The same page says you will not spoil a child by holding or responding. That line is the US agency's own wording on one age page. It is not a result from a named experiment, and it does not set a rule for older children.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US government work, public domain. Supports the tips that cuddling helps the baby feel safe and cared for and that holding or responding will not spoil the baby.
